# Build the Wall, Carry the Sword

## Scripture
"Nehemiah said, 'Go and enjoy choice food and sweet drinks, and send some to those who have nothing prepared. This day is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.'" – Nehemiah 8:10

## Reflection
Nehemiah knew what it meant to work under pressure. He rebuilt Jerusalem's walls with a sword strapped to his side and a trowel in his hand, expecting attack at any moment. Yet when the people were exhausted and weeping under conviction, he didn't tell them to grind harder. He told them to feast. Why? Because joy—not grit alone—is where a man's real strength lives.

Too many of us try to white-knuckle our faith. We muscle through quiet times, force discipline, and treat God like a demanding boss. That approach burns out fast. The strength Nehemiah pointed to wasn't manufactured by willpower; it flowed from delight in the Lord. A man who genuinely rejoices in God fights differently. His discipline has a heartbeat. His endurance has a source deeper than caffeine and ego.

So today, don't just endure your training or your walk with Christ. Rejoice in it. Let gratitude fuel the grind. Joy is not weakness—it's the engine.

## Daily Challenge
Do 3 rounds of 15 pushups, pausing between sets to thank God out loud for one specific blessing. Let joy carry your reps.
